title: In four fly connectomes, PFL3 goal-heading offsets near +-70 degrees and PFL2 offsets near 180 degrees repeat, and each PFL3 offset sign gives its descending output side (83/83)
abstract: Question: fly PFL3 neurons compare heading (protocerebral bridge, PB) with a goal (FC2 input in the fan-shaped body, FB) and drive the steering neuron DNa02; PFL2 neurons drive DNa03. Physiology and one connectome (hemibrain) give offsets of about +-67.5 degrees for PFL3 and 180 degrees for PFL2. Do this geometry and the wiring that makes the goal attractive repeat in other animals? Data: hemibrain v1.2, FlyWire 783, male CNS v1.0 and BANC 888 (four animals, both sexes, FIB-SEM and TEM); 24-25 PFL3 and 12 PFL2 per map; no new downloads. Method: label-free PB phases from EPG and EPG-Delta7 input; FB phases from FC2 input, with FC2 phases from balanced left and right PFN input; frame turn direction from the PEN shift sign and published PEN turn asymmetry; offset = FB - PB; rate read-out of turn drive; Poisson synapse resampling (150 per map); FB-phase permutation null. Validation: PB phases match glomerulus labels (R 0.88-0.98); FB phases match column labels at -41.5 degrees per column (R 0.96-0.97). Results: PFL3 populations sit at -58 to -76 and +63 to +76 degrees (separation 126-151; model 135) and PFL2 is 174-178 degrees from the PFL3 midpoint in all maps. The offset sign of each PFL3 neuron agrees with the side of its DNa02/DNa03 output in 83 of 83 neurons (12/12, 24/24, 24/24, 23/23), including 9 irregular neurons whose PB side breaks the population rule. With unit DN weights, every map has one stable steering point within 2.5 degrees of the goal (95% intervals within -6 to +17 degrees) and an unstable point at 169-180 degrees; permuted FB phases give one-fifth of the turn signal (p = 0.001). PFL2 drive peaks at 173-178 degrees. Measured DNa02 synapse imbalances (-4% to +11%) bias the stable point by up to 13 degrees. Limitations: one animal per map; synapse counts as weights; no activity data; the FB frame assumes symmetric PFN shifts; between-map differences exceed synapse-count intervals and are not explained; hemibrain lacks the left LAL.

display.caption: Offset (FB phase minus PB phase) of every PFL3 and PFL2 neuron in four connectomes. Blue up-triangles: PFL3 with output to the left DNa02/DNa03; orange down-triangles: right; black edges: neurons whose DN side breaks the PB-side rule; open circles: hemibrain neurons without visible DN output (left LAL outside the volume); aqua squares: PFL2. Dashed lines: +-67.5 and 180 degrees.

Rate read-out of each connectome. Top: PFL3 turn drive (left minus right DN; positive = left turn) against heading minus goal, unit weights by DN side (solid) and measured DNa02 synapses (dotted); dot and bar: stable point and its 95% synapse-resampling interval. Bottom: PFL2 drive to DNa03, which peaks when the heading is opposite to the goal.
PB phase (heading input) against FB phase (goal input via FC2) of each PFL neuron, label-free, in a common heading frame per connectome. Dashed lines: FB = PB +67.5, PB -67.5 and PB +180 degrees.
